contents.content:
Six different job types, one notification, 388 posts total - the Himachal Pradesh High Court in Shimla has put this out. At the top sits Court Manager, at the bottom Safai Karmchari, and in between you've got Clerk, Stenographer, Driver and Process Server. Forms went live 10 August 2026 and shut on 10 September 2026 (Advt. No. HHC/Recruit./DJ-Misc./2024-I).

Worth saying upfront: eligibility isn't uniform here. A Court Manager needs an MBA plus three years of management experience. A Peon just needs 10+2. Check which post you're going for in the table below first.

Age Limit as on 01/01/2026

  • Court Manager (Group-B) : 25 to 35 Years
  • All Other Posts (Group-C & Group-D) : 18 to 45 Years
  • Age Relaxation Applicable as per Himachal Pradesh Government Regulations

How to Fill Himachal Pradesh High Court Various Post Online Form 2026

The portal usually slows down in the last few days before the deadline, so it's better not to wait until the first week of September. Eligibility rules differ enough across these six posts that reading the notification properly matters more than usual here.

  • Gather educational certificates, typing or stenography certificates where relevant, driving license for the Driver post, and ID and address proof before opening the form.
  • Photo, signature and ID scans need to match the size and format the portal specifies.
  • Go through the preview screen carefully. Corrections after final submission are not always simple.
  • The form is not counted as submitted until the fee is paid, so don't leave that step for later.
  • Save the confirmation page somewhere you can find it again.

Himachal Pradesh High Court Various Post Preparation Tips 2026

  • Typing and shorthand speed don't improve overnight. Clerk and Stenographer applicants should be practicing daily starting now, not two weeks before the exam.
  • Kruti Dev-10 is not the Hindi keyboard layout most people grow up typing on. Anyone used to Unicode or Mangal should spend real time on Kruti Dev specifically, rather than assuming the speed will transfer automatically.
  • The Court Manager post reads more like a mid-level admin role than a clerical one. HR, finance and process management basics matter more here than general GK.
  • Drivers should sort their license category and experience proof well in advance. A mismatch is one of the more common reasons documents get rejected during verification.
  • Process Server and Group-D applicants should watch for whether a written screening gets added alongside the merit list. Either way, a quick revision of general awareness and basic reasoning won't hurt.

Court Manager is different from the rest here - that post wants candidates aged 25 to 35. Everything else (Clerk, Stenographer, Driver, Process Server, Group-D) runs on the wider 18 to 45 band, all as on 01 January 2026.

IBPS has thrown open the 16th edition of its clerical recruitment drive - CRP CSA-XVI - with 11,403 indicative vacancies for the Customer Service Associate post (the role most people still call "Clerk") across 11 participating public sector banks. Online registration runs from 1 August to 21 August 2026, covering hiring for the 2027-28 vacancy cycle.

This is a state/UT-wise recruitment, meaning you can apply against vacancies in only one state or union territory, so it's worth checking where the opportunities actually sit before you register.

Important Dates

Short Notice Released 27/07/2026
Detailed Notification / Application Begin 01/08/2026
Last Date for Apply Online 21/08/2026
Last Date Pay Exam Fee 21/08/2026
Prelims Exam Date 10 & 11 October 2026
Mains Exam Date 27 December 2026
Provisional Allotment March 2027

Application Fee

  • General / OBC / EWS : 850/- (Inclusive of GST)
  • SC / ST / PwBD / ESM : 175/- (Inclusive of GST)
  • Fee Is Non-Refundable Once Paid
  • Pay Through Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking or UPI Only - Bank Transaction Charges, if Any, Are Borne by the Candidate

Age Limit as on 01/08/2026

  • Minimum Age : 20 Years
  • Maximum Age : 28 Years
  • Age Relaxation : SC/ST - 5 Years, OBC-NCL - 3 Years, PwBD - 10 Years, Ex-Servicemen - 5 Years (Cumulative With Only One Other Applicable Category)

Selection Process

There's no interview at any stage of this recruitment - selection runs purely on your Prelims and Mains scores, followed by document verification. One thing that trips up a lot of first-time applicants: your Prelims marks don't carry forward into the final merit list. Prelims only decides who gets shortlisted for Mains; the Mains score alone determines your final rank.

  • Preliminary Examination - 100 Questions / 100 Marks / 60 Minutes, Split Into English (30Q), Numerical Ability (35Q) and Reasoning Ability (35Q), Each With a 20-Minute Sectional Time Limit
  • Main Examination - 160 Questions / 200 Marks / 125 Minutes, Covering General/Financial Awareness (40Q/50M), General English (40Q/40M), Reasoning Ability (40Q/60M) and Quantitative Aptitude (40Q/50M)
  • Document Verification for Candidates Provisionally Allotted a Bank

Pay Scale

Basic pay for the Customer Service Associate post starts at Rs. 24,050 and progresses to Rs. 64,480 over the course of increments. With allowances added in, the starting gross salary typically works out to around Rs. 40,000-42,000 a month, though this varies slightly by posting location.

How to Fill IBPS Clerk CRP CSA-XVI Online Form 2026

  • Visit ibps.in, Open the CRP CSA-XVI Section and Click "New Registration" to Generate Your Provisional Registration Number and Password.
  • Upload Your Photograph, Signature, Left Thumb Impression, Handwritten Declaration and 10th/SSLC Certificate as per the Format Specified in Annexure IV of the Notification.
  • Fill the Form Section by Section Using "Save and Next," Since Saving Partway Through Lets You Come Back Without Losing Progress.
  • Pay the Fee Within the Same 01-21 August Window - a Saved but Unpaid Form Is Treated as an Invalid Application.
  • Double-Check That Your Payment Actually Went Through Before Closing the Tab - This Is a Common Point Where Applications Get Missed.
  • Print the Final Application Form and the Payment Receipt for Your Records.

IBPS Clerk CRP CSA-XVI Preparation Tips 2026

  • Since Prelims Marks Don't Count Toward the Final Merit, Treat It as a Speed Test - Focus on Clearing Sectional Cutoffs Comfortably Rather Than Maximizing Your Score There.
  • Mains Is Where the Real Battle Happens - Quantitative Aptitude and Reasoning Together Carry 110 of the 200 Marks, So Prioritize Them in Your Daily Practice.
  • For General/Financial Awareness, Track Recent RBI Policy Changes, Repo Rate Movements and Major Banking Sector News From the Last 4-6 Months.
  • Work on Speed in English - With Only 35 Minutes for 40 Questions in Mains, Reading Comprehension Passages Need to Be Tackled Efficiently, Not Read Word by Word.
  • Practice Local Language Basics if It Isn't Your Mother Tongue, Since Proficiency in the State/UT's Local Language Is a Stated Eligibility Requirement.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the last date to apply for IBPS Clerk CRP CSA-XVI 2026?

The last date to apply online, along with the fee payment deadline, is 21 August 2026.

A total of 11,403 indicative vacancies have been announced across participating states and union territories, though this figure may change once Union Bank of India reports its numbers.

No, there is no interview. Selection is based entirely on the Preliminary and Main Examination scores, followed by document verification.

Do Prelims marks count toward the final selection?

No, Prelims is only a qualifying stage to shortlist candidates for Mains. The final merit list is prepared solely on the basis of Mains marks.

What is the application fee for IBPS Clerk 2026?

General, OBC and EWS candidates need to pay Rs. 850/-, while SC, ST, PwBD and Ex-Servicemen candidates pay Rs. 175/-, both figures inclusive of GST.

Can a candidate apply for vacancies in more than one state?

No, recruitment under CRP CSA-XVI is conducted state/UT-wise, and a candidate can apply for vacancies in only one state or union territory.

What is the age limit for IBPS Clerk CRP CSA-XVI 2026?

Candidates must be between 20 and 28 years of age as on 01 August 2026, with standard age relaxation applicable for reserved categories.

Q9. Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'Solvent' (in a financial context):

Q10. Identify the grammatically correct sentence for use in a formal banking communication:

  • Kindly revert back to us at your earliest convenience.

Q11. A sum of Rs. 12,000 is invested at compound interest, compounded annually, and grows to Rs. 13,230 in 2 years. What is the annual rate of interest?

  • A prepaid negotiable instrument issued by a bank, payable on demand at a specified branch

Q22. If MONEY is coded numerically based on reverse alphabet position (Z=1, Y=2...A=26) and DEPOSIT needs the same coding, what would be the code for the letter 'D' in DEPOSIT?

Q24. A sum is divided between A and B such that A's share, invested at 8% simple interest, and B's share, invested at 10% simple interest, yield equal annual interest. If the total sum is Rs. 9000, what is A's share?

The last date to apply online is 07 August 2026.

How many total vacancies are there in this apprentice recruitment?

A total of 1853 posts have been announced for Various Trade Apprentice positions.

Is there an application fee for SC/ST and female candidates?

No, SC/ST candidates and all category female candidates are exempted from the application fee.

What is the minimum qualification required for RRC Prayagraj Apprentice posts?

Candidates need a Class 10 pass certificate with minimum 50% marks along with an ITI/NCVT certificate in a related trade.

No, selection is based on a merit list prepared from Class 10 and ITI marks, followed by document verification.

What is the age limit for RRC Prayagraj Apprentice Recruitment 2026?

Candidates must be between 15 and 24 years of age as on 07 July 2026, with age relaxation as per rules.

The complete trade-wise and division-wise vacancy details are provided in the official notification released by RRC Prayagraj.

WBPSC ICDS Supervisor - Job Specific Practice Questions (ICDS Scheme, Anganwadi Structure & Social Welfare)

25 Objective Questions with Explanation

Q1. An ICDS Supervisor is generally responsible for overseeing how many Anganwadi Centres on average in a project area?

  • 5 to 8
  • Around 20 to 25
  • 50 to 60
  • 100 and above

Explanation: A Supervisor (also called Mukhya Sevika) typically monitors around 20-25 Anganwadi Centres under one ICDS project/circle, conducting regular visits, checking registers and guiding the Anganwadi Workers.

Q2. Which register is NOT usually maintained at an Anganwadi Centre?

  • Growth Monitoring Register
  • Attendance Register
  • Beneficiary Register (Pregnant/Lactating Women)
  • Land Revenue Register

Explanation: Anganwadi records mainly track children, mothers, health check-ups, nutrition and attendance - not land revenue, which falls under a different department entirely.

Q3. The Take Home Ration (THR) under ICDS is generally provided to which beneficiaries?

  • Only school-going children above 10 years
  • Children 6 months to 3 years, and pregnant/lactating mothers
  • Only senior citizens
  • Only Anganwadi staff

Explanation: THR is meant for children who cannot yet eat cooked meals at the centre (6 months to 3 years) and for pregnant and lactating mothers, so they can consume nutrition at home.

Q4. Which of these is a core service under the ICDS package (also called the "Six Services")?

  • Vocational Skill Training for Adults
  • Non-Formal Pre-School Education
  • Loan Distribution
  • Pension Disbursement

Explanation: The ICDS "six services" are supplementary nutrition, immunization, health check-up, referral services, non-formal pre-school education, and nutrition & health education.

Q5. Who is the immediate reporting authority above an ICDS Supervisor at the block level in West Bengal?

  • Child Development Project Officer (CDPO)
  • District Magistrate
  • Block Development Officer only
  • State Secretary

Explanation: The CDPO heads the ICDS project at the block level and Supervisors report to the CDPO, who further reports up the district and state administrative chain.

Q6. Which tool is commonly used by Anganwadi Workers to assess a child's nutritional status during growth monitoring?

  • Weighing scale and height chart against growth cards
  • Blood pressure monitor
  • ECG machine
  • X-ray machine

Explanation: Growth monitoring under ICDS relies on regular weight and height recording, plotted against standard growth cards to identify malnourished or at-risk children early.

Q7. Which category of children is specifically prioritized for referral to a Nutrition Rehabilitation Centre (NRC)?

  • Children with normal growth
  • Severely Acute Malnourished (SAM) children
  • Children above 12 years
  • Only children with eye problems

Explanation: SAM children need intensive medical and nutritional care, so ICDS field staff refer them to NRCs where they receive supervised treatment until their condition stabilizes.

Q8. The Scheme for Adolescent Girls under the Women & Child Development set-up mainly targets which age group?

  • 0 to 3 years
  • 3 to 6 years
  • 11 to 14 years (out-of-school girls in most versions)
  • Above 25 years

Explanation: This scheme focuses on nutrition, health awareness, and life-skill support for adolescent girls, particularly those who have dropped out of formal schooling.

Q9. Which of the following comes under the Social Welfare Department's mandate along with ICDS in West Bengal?

  • Welfare schemes for differently-abled persons and destitute women
  • Highway construction
  • Power distribution
  • Railway ticketing

Explanation: Along with child and maternal welfare, the department also runs programs for the differently-abled, orphaned children, and destitute or distressed women.

Q10. What does the term "VHSND" (commonly linked with Anganwadi activities) stand for?

  • Village Health, Sanitation and Nutrition Day
  • Vocational Health Skill Naming Drive
  • Village Housing Scheme for Nutrition Development
  • Village Health Survey and Numbering Data

Explanation: VHSND is a monthly outreach event held at the Anganwadi level, bringing together ASHA, ANM and Anganwadi Workers for immunization, health check-ups and nutrition counselling.

Q11. As per general ICDS norms, what is the minimum number of days an Anganwadi Centre should ideally remain functional in a month?

  • 10 days
  • 15 days
  • 25 days
  • 30 days, no holidays

Explanation: Anganwadi Centres are generally expected to function around 25 days a month, excluding weekly offs and government holidays, to keep nutrition and pre-school activities consistent.

Q12. Which of these duties would typically fall to a Supervisor rather than an Anganwadi Worker?

  • Serving cooked meals daily
  • Conducting on-the-spot inspection and verifying stock registers
  • Cleaning the centre premises
  • Taking daily attendance of children

Explanation: Field-level duties like cooking or attendance are handled by the Worker/Helper, while inspection, verification, and guidance across multiple centres fall under the Supervisor's role.

Q13. The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme is administered in coordination with which ministries?

  • Women & Child Development, Health, and Education
  • Defence and Home Affairs
  • Railways and Civil Aviation
  • Commerce and Industry

Explanation: Since the scheme addresses declining child sex ratio and girls' education together, it is run jointly through the WCD, Health and Education ministries.

Q14. Under the Mid-Day Meal / nutrition linkage, which age group is generally NOT covered by the Anganwadi feeding programme but by school-based schemes instead?

  • 6 months to 3 years
  • 3 to 6 years
  • Primary school-going children (6+ years)
  • Pregnant women

Explanation: Once a child moves into formal primary schooling, nutrition support generally shifts from the Anganwadi's supplementary feeding to the school Mid-Day Meal Scheme.

Q15. What is the primary purpose of the Nutrition and Health Education (NHE) component of ICDS?

  • Building awareness among mothers on childcare, hygiene and diet practices
  • Providing free housing loans
  • Distributing agricultural equipment
  • Conducting driving license tests

Explanation: NHE sessions equip mothers and caregivers with practical knowledge on feeding practices, hygiene, and preventive healthcare for children and themselves.

Q16. Which of the following is generally a disqualifying factor while filling the WBPSC ICDS application, unless specifically permitted?

  • Providing false information in the OTR profile
  • Applying from a cyber café
  • Uploading photo in JPEG format
  • Applying a day before the deadline

Explanation: Submitting incorrect or false details in the One Time Registration profile can lead to rejection of candidature at any later stage of the recruitment process.

Q17. In the ICDS structure, what is the role of an "Anganwadi Helper" distinct from a "Worker"?

  • Assisting with meal preparation, cleanliness and bringing children to the centre
  • Handling the block-level budget
  • Approving maternity benefit applications
  • Conducting the Supervisor's exam

Explanation: The Helper supports the Worker with day-to-day physical tasks at the centre, while planning, teaching and record-keeping remain the Worker's responsibility.

Q18. A batch of registers at an Anganwadi Centre shows 60 enrolled children, of whom 45 attended on a given day. What is the attendance percentage that day?

  • 65%
  • 70%
  • 75%
  • 80%

Explanation: 45 out of 60 = 45/60 x 100 = 75%. Such register-based percentage calculation questions are common in the ICDS Prelims arithmetic section.

Q19. If a Supervisor covers 24 Anganwadi Centres in 6 working days, visiting an equal number each day, how many centres does she cover per day?

  • 2
  • 3
  • 4
  • 6

Explanation: 24 centres divided across 6 days = 4 centres per day, a straightforward division-based question framed around real field duties.

Q20. A nutrition budget of ₹1,20,000 is to be distributed equally among 8 Anganwadi Centres in a circle. How much does each centre receive?

  • ₹12,000
  • ₹15,000
  • ₹16,000
  • ₹18,000

Explanation: ₹1,20,000 ÷ 8 = ₹15,000 per centre. Budget-distribution style word problems are frequently framed around welfare-department scenarios in this exam.

Q21. Out of 200 children screened during a growth monitoring drive, 15% were found moderately underweight. How many children does that represent?

  • 25
  • 30
  • 35
  • 40

Explanation: 15% of 200 = 30 children. Percentage-based questions tied to health screening data are a common format in the ICDS/Social Welfare paper.

Q22. If Anganwadi Worker, Helper, and Supervisor posts are advertised in the ratio 6:3:1, and there are 60 Worker posts, how many Supervisor posts are there?

  • 8
  • 10
  • 12
  • 15

Explanation: If 6 parts = 60, then 1 part = 10, so Supervisor posts (1 part) = 10. Ratio questions like this reflect how vacancy break-ups are often presented in real notifications.

Q23. A Supervisor starts her centre visits from the CDPO office, travels east to Centre A, then turns south to reach Centre B. In which direction must she travel to return directly to the CDPO office?

  • South-East
  • North-West
  • South-West
  • North-East

Explanation: Moving east then south takes her away from the start point diagonally; the direct return path would be the opposite diagonal, i.e. north-west.

Q24. In a coded register, "AWC" (Anganwadi Centre) is written as "CYE" by shifting each letter forward by 2. Using the same logic, how would "CDPO" be coded?

  • DERP
  • EFRQ
  • EFQR
  • DFRQ

Explanation: Shifting each letter of C-D-P-O forward by 2 gives E-F-R-Q, following the same +2 pattern used to convert AWC into CYE.

Q25. Four documents are required for the ICDS application: Domicile Certificate, Educational Certificate, Caste Certificate, and Nutrition Chart. Which one does NOT belong with the rest in this list?

  • Domicile Certificate
  • Educational Certificate
  • Caste Certificate
  • Nutrition Chart

Explanation: The first three are personal eligibility documents needed at the time of applying; a Nutrition Chart is a field-level ICDS record, not an application document.
